correctness.rationale: Forcing chains partition the 2k pendant vertices into chains having at most two pendants each, so any k-vertex minimum start is leaf-only. A forced hub first requires a 111 triple; chain endpoints imply exactly one such hub force. After hub coloration, zero-index rim vertices can only be seeded by neighboring 11 selected rims and propagated across isolated selected rims; all but one zero component must be seeded, and the final unseeded singleton is the physical 000. This is equivalent to one adjacent equal-type pair of each defect kind with all other defects alternating. Marking the unique 11 pair and distributing odd alternating gaps gives N_k=2k sum_{r>=2}(r-1) binom(k-2,2r-3) and hence 6 (k=3) or k^2 2^(k-4) (k>=4). Independent zero-forcing closure enumerated all leaf-balanced subsets for n=6,8,10,12,14 giving 6,16,50,144,392, confirming boundaries; full proof addresses unbounded k. The slide graph is edgeless because a leaf slide necessarily gives an internal selected vertex.
residual_risks: Finite counts verify small cases only; the chain and defect-component arguments supply the all-k theorem.
No independent full C++ run n=6..20; both checkers inspected.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general forcing-chain path-cover bound gives k and leaf rigidity but not the defect combinatorics. Circular-ladder results classify a prism with two cycles, not a wheel-plus-pendants helm.

value.rationale: The even helms are a natural infinite graph family already studied for zero forcing; exact enumeration and an if-and-only-if local defect description of every minimum configuration are significant structural invariants. They enable reconfiguration and sampling analyses and are not obtained from the known zero forcing number. The slide-isolation is a transparent but legitimate corollary, not the sole value.

final_claim: For the even helm graph with n=2k>=6 rim vertices, every minimum standard zero-forcing set is leaf-only; the exact number is 6 for k=3 and k^2*2^(k-4) for k>=4, characterized by one physically consecutive double 00 and 11 defect in an otherwise alternating cyclic binary word; its minimum-set token-slide graph is edgeless.
limitations: The argument applies to even n>=6 only and ordinary zero forcing; no odd-helm or all-size forcing polynomial is claimed.
